summary: Netanyahu's bloc leads the count but is short of 61, and so is Eisenkot's. Democrats leader Yair Golan wants the change bloc to govern with the Arab parties, but that majority only exists with Yisrael Beiteinu, and Liberman ruled out both Arab parties and minority governments during the campaign. Eisenkot has promised a 'Zionist government' and has not endorsed Golan's idea. Every path to 61 right now requires at least one leader to break a campaign pledge.

phase.next: Official results by Nov 4. President Herzog then has seven days to choose who gets the first try at forming a government, who then has 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners. Without a majority, Netanyahu needs defectors or a new partner from the other side.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu rather than join him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Proposed by Yair Golan on Oct 28. Without Yisrael Beiteinu the same group falls short, so Liberman decides whether this exists.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am, the Joint List and any minority government.
Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Abbas says both camps have contacted him, but this falls short of 61 even before Liberman's veto.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it in two.

blockers.text: Shas and UTJ say they won't join any government unless yeshiva students' exemptions are written into law.
Liberman ruled out Shas and UTJ.
Eisenkot's core promise is national service for all.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: Analysts call it Netanyahu's most realistic route, at the cost of dropping Ben-Gvir and possibly the Haredi parties. Who would lead it is the sticking point.

blockers.text: Eisenkot says Netanyahu should step down.
Liberman won't sit with Likud while Netanyahu leads it.
Ben-Gvir warned Netanyahu against a unity government with Eisenkot.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu Plus Bennett's Together
scenarios.note: Ideologically the closest fit, but Bennett and Lapid campaigned on replacing Netanyahu.

blockers.text: Bennett declared on election night that Netanyahu has lost.

מחל.stance: Wants a right-wing national government; calls relying on anti-Zionist Arab parties unthinkable.
red_lines: No government that depends on Arab parties

דרך.stance: Eisenkot vows to form a 'Zionist government that drafts everyone' and says Netanyahu should step down.

רק.stance: Bennett says 'Netanyahu has lost' and that talks among opposition leaders are underway.

אמת.stance: Golan urges a change government in partnership with the Arab parties: '65 is more than 55.'

ל.stance: Liberman urges Likud MKs to revolt and expects soldiers' votes to lift his party.

שס.stance: Won't join any government unless yeshiva students' draft exemptions are written into law.

ג.stance: Asher set the same condition as Shas: a law securing yeshiva students' exemptions.

ב.stance: Ben-Gvir rejects a unity government with Eisenkot as a 'government of paralysis.'

ט.stance: No public post-election statement on coalition terms found yet.

עם.stance: Abbas says both camps are talking to him; open to an Eisenkot-led government once it has the numbers.

ודם.stance: Leaders say they will back efforts to stop Netanyahu and support an opposition-led coalition.
